expectations.text: The first substantive action is a summary of what is already known about the user (memory/context scan)
expectations.evidence: Response opens directly with analysis: 'You're describing a classic manager stuck in execution mode problem.' No memory scan or context summary step.

expectations.text: Discovery questions are presented one at a time, not as a numbered list in a single response
expectations.evidence: No discovery questions are asked at all. The response goes straight to recommendations without interviewing the user.

expectations.text: The individual lens is selected or inferred (not organizational)
expectations.evidence: No lens framework is used. The response implicitly focuses on individual workflows but does not name or select a lens.

expectations.text: The report identifies at least 3 concrete, distinct opportunities
expectations.evidence: Response identifies 5 areas: Campaign Performance Reporting, Monthly Board Deck, Content Review and Feedback, Meeting Notes and Follow-ups, Email and Communication Drafting. All are concrete and distinct.

expectations.text: At least 2 of the opportunities are specific to marketing workflows (e.g., campaign reporting, content review, board deck) rather than generic AI advice
expectations.evidence: 3 of 5 are marketing-specific: Campaign Performance Reporting (HubSpot/GA), Monthly Board Deck (pipeline metrics), Content Review (brand voice checklist). Meeting Notes and Email Drafting are role-generic.

expectations.text: The report contains the required Report Header with Role, Date, Lens, and Opportunities Identified fields
expectations.evidence: No structured report header. Response uses a simple H1 title 'Where AI Can Help You as a Marketing Manager' with no metadata table.

expectations.text: The report includes a Top Recommendations section listing the top 3 opportunities in priority order
expectations.evidence: Response includes a '## Priority Order' section listing all 5 items in priority order with brief rationales. Not titled 'Top Recommendations' but serves the same purpose.

expectations.text: After presenting the report, the user is asked to pick workflow candidates
expectations.evidence: Response ends with 'Want me to help you set up any of these? I'd suggest starting with the campaign reporting dashboard since it's the quickest win.' This is a generic offer to help, not a structured candidate selection for a downstream framework step.

suggestions.assertion: The report includes a Top Recommendations section listing the top 3 opportunities in priority order
suggestions.reason: This passed for the without-skill run because the response has a 'Priority Order' section — a reasonable response will naturally prioritize. Consider checking for the specific section title or checking that it's limited to top 3 (not all items).

eval_feedback.overall: Good discrimination overall. The process assertions (memory scan, one-at-a-time questions, lens selection) are the strongest discriminators between with-skill and without-skill runs. Content quality assertions (3+ opportunities, marketing-specificity) pass in both cases — they test baseline competence, not skill value-add.
